notes: Averages of 2016–2025, from Météo-France's SAFRAN reanalysis (8 km daily grid), weighted by where the commune's residents live. Temperatures are corrected month by month from the grid cell's mean altitude to theirs, fitted on Météo-France stations.
Highest and lowest are the extremes of these ten years, not all-time records. Mean maximum is the average of each month's (or year's) single hottest day; mean minimum likewise for the coldest.
Solar energy stands in for sunshine hours, which only ~190 stations measure. As a guide, 1,050 kWh/m² a year is about 1,800–1,900 hours of sun, 1,600 about 2,800–2,900.
Rainfall is not corrected for altitude: in a sheltered mountain valley the grid can overstate it. On the Mediterranean shore, sea breezes keep summer highs lower than an 8 km cell reaching inland.
